metadata.purpose: Define the foundational operating model, execution architecture, inheritance mechanism, lifecycle governance, conflict resolution, dependency management, and traceability framework for the Pipeline Assessment Rules Engine. Version 1.1 adds an additive SWOT Intelligence integration layer while preserving the existing assessment phases and their authoritative responsibilities.
metadata.designPrinciple: Deterministic rules govern assessment calculation, validation, decision execution, lifecycle management, and governance, while AI reasoning provides interpretation, diagnosis, and recommendation intelligence.

inheritanceArchitecture.model: Universal Baseline + Revenue Motion Override + Industry Override
inheritanceArchitecture.fallbackBehavior: When no specific override exists, inherit the lower-level rule definition.

releaseNotes.preservationPolicy: Existing v1.0 rule definitions, identifiers, scoring thresholds, outputs, lifecycle behavior, risk engine and winning strategy engine are preserved except for the explicitly documented dependency clarification.

sourceAssets.role: Approved evidence objects, evidence-to-SWOT mappings and integration contracts
Approved SWOT factor definitions, inheritance, evaluation, TOWS and governance

ruleEngineIdentity.primaryFunction: Execute assessment, scoring, calculation, validation, risk, recommendation prioritization, lifecycle, and governance rules.

ruleExecutionModel.executionPrinciple: Rules execute according to dependency order to ensure upstream validation and calculation accuracy before downstream decisions.

executionSequence.description: Resolve pipeline context, revenue motion, industry, and active configuration.
Validate inherited data and assessment input completeness.
Evaluate evidence eligibility, quality, confidence, and relevance.
Calculate PADF dimension conditions and health states.
Apply dependency, reinforcement, contradiction, and constraint rules.
Calculate pipeline winability and overall health.
Detect, classify, and aggregate pipeline risks.
Identify eligible strategies and prioritize recommendations.
Update pipeline evolution status and historical records.

ruleCategories.purpose: Validate input, evidence, and data quality.

rulePriorityLevels.meaning: Critical blocking rule. Failure prevents assessment continuation.

layers.purpose: Common rules applicable across all revenue motions and industries.
Adjust rules according to revenue motion characteristics.
Adjust rules according to industry-specific buying behavior, risk, and evidence requirements.

inheritanceResolutionRules.condition: An industry override exists for the applicable rule.
No industry override exists and a revenue motion override exists.
inheritanceResolutionRules.action: Apply the revenue motion-specific rule definition.

inheritanceResolutionRules.condition: Neither an industry override nor a revenue motion override exists.
inheritanceResolutionRules.action: Apply the universal baseline rule definition.

conflictResolutionPrinciples.description: More specific industry rules override broader revenue motion and universal rules.
When rules at the same inheritance level conflict, the higher-priority rule takes precedence.
Mandatory audit, traceability, and governance controls cannot be overridden by business rules.
Material rule conflicts must be logged and traceable rather than silently resolved.

resolutionSequence: Record the resolution decision in the execution trace.

dependencyModel.purpose: Ensure rules execute only after required prerequisite rules have successfully completed.

dependencyClarificationV1_1.issue: The v1.0 global dependency statement implied that winability calculation required risk evaluation while Phase 7 risk evaluation depended on Phase 6 winability outputs.
dependencyClarificationV1_1.resolution: Phase 6 calculates base winability. Phase 7 performs risk evaluation and calculates risk-adjusted winability. Phase 8 consumes risk-adjusted winability.
dependencyClarificationV1_1.preservation: Existing Phase 6 base winability calculation methodology and Phase 7 risk adjustment rules remain authoritative.

ruleStates.description: Rule under development and not eligible for production execution.
Rule undergoing functional and business validation.
Rule approved and available for production execution.
Rule replaced by a newer rule but retained for historical compatibility.
Rule permanently removed from executable rule sets.

majorVersionChange: Material change to rule execution behavior

ruleExecutionTraceability.traceabilityPrinciple: Every material assessment conclusion must be traceable to the rule chain, evidence references, configuration context, and rule versions that produced the result.

rules.condition: A rule is executed by the Pipeline Assessment Rules Engine.
rules.action: Create an execution trace entry for the rule execution.
Require authorization, justification, and audit logging.
rules.output: Override is explicitly governed and traceable.

rules.action: Block calculation until required inputs satisfy validation requirements.
rules.output: Calculation proceeds only with validated inputs.

rules.condition: A rule requires industry, revenue motion, or other configuration context.
rules.action: Use the resolved configuration context associated with the pipeline assessment.
rules.output: Rule execution uses a consistent configuration context.

rules.condition: An assessment snapshot has been committed to historical records.
rules.action: Prevent modification of the original snapshot and preserve subsequent changes as new assessment events or snapshots.

Opportunity Qualification status does not indicate a qualified opportunity.

pipelineEligibilityRules.action: Prevent creation of a new active assessment and route the pipeline to lifecycle handling.

Resolve the solution, offering, or product context associated with the pipeline.
Inherit and resolve the buying context established during Opportunity Qualification.
Inherit and resolve the known stakeholder context from Opportunity Qualification.

inheritedDataValidationRules.action: Validate that the pipeline originates from a completed Opportunity Qualification process.
Validate and inherit the revenue motion assigned during Opportunity Qualification.
Validate and inherit the industry classification assigned during Opportunity Qualification.

phaseDefinition.purpose: Define the deterministic rules for identifying, validating, qualifying, normalizing, and evaluating pipeline assessment evidence before the evidence is used by downstream PADF dimension assessment rules.

principles.description: Assessment conclusions must be grounded in identifiable evidence rather than unsupported assumptions.
Every evaluated evidence item must retain a traceable source reference.
Evidence must be evaluated against the pipeline context, revenue motion, industry, and applicable assessment dimension.
Evidence quality must be distinguished from evidence existence.
Current and temporally relevant evidence should receive stronger qualification status than stale evidence.
Independent corroborating evidence increases confidence in an assessment conclusion.
Conflicting evidence must not be silently discarded and must remain visible to downstream reasoning.
Absence of evidence must not automatically be interpreted as evidence of an unfavorable condition.

evidenceIdentificationRules.action: Retrieve evidence expectations and evidence mappings applicable to the resolved revenue motion, industry, pipeline context, and PADF dimensions.
Retrieve applicable evidence references inherited from Opportunity Qualification.
Identify newly submitted evidence generated or collected during Pipeline Assessment.

evidenceInheritanceRules.action: Preserve the original Opportunity Qualification evidence reference and source attribution.
Do not overwrite the original qualification evidence record when using it within Pipeline Assessment.
Allow inherited evidence to be reevaluated for its relevance, freshness, strength, and applicability to the current pipeline assessment context.

evidenceEligibilityRules.action: Allow the evidence object to enter the evaluation process.
Allow evidence evaluation only when the source is identifiable.
Allow evidence evaluation only when evidence content is present.
Exclude the evidence from qualified evidence used by downstream assessment rules.

output.ineligibilityReason: Required evidence attributes are missing or invalid.

evidenceRelevanceRules.action: Evaluate whether the evidence directly supports one or more applicable PADF dimensions.
Classify the evidence as indirect or contextual evidence when it provides relevant supporting information without directly demonstrating pipeline conditions.

evidenceSourceRules.action: Classify the evidence as first-party or directly attributable evidence.
Classify the evidence as third-party or externally sourced evidence.
Mark the evidence as unverified and prevent it from receiving maximum evidence confidence.

evidenceQualityRules.action: Evaluate whether the evidence contains specific, concrete information rather than generic statements.
Evaluate whether the evidence can be independently verified or traced to a reliable source.
Evaluate whether the evidence contains measurable values, dates, financial information, volumes, milestones, or other concrete indicators.
Evaluate whether the evidence provides information directly related to the customer's decision process.

evidenceFreshnessRules.action: Use the evidence date to evaluate evidence freshness.
Classify evidence as aging and reduce its confidence contribution according to applicable evidence configuration.
Classify evidence as stale and prevent it from being treated as current evidence.

evidenceStrengthRules.action: Determine evidence strength using source quality, relevance, specificity, verifiability, freshness, and corroboration factors.
Classify the evidence as strong evidence when supporting quality factors are satisfied.
Classify evidence as moderate when it provides meaningful but incomplete or less direct support.
Classify the evidence as weak unless stronger corroborating evidence supports the same conclusion.

evidenceCorroborationRules.action: Identify independent evidence items supporting the same assessment conclusion.
Increase evidence confidence when independent corroborating evidence supports the same conclusion.
Classify the evidence as single-source evidence without applying a corroboration uplift.

evidenceContradictionRules.action: Flag the affected evidence group for contradiction handling and prevent automatic resolution of the conflicting conclusion.
Identify the stronger evidence based on source reliability, relevance, freshness, specificity, and verifiability while retaining the contradictory evidence reference.
Retain the contradiction as unresolved and require downstream assessment reasoning to account for the uncertainty.

evidenceCompletenessRules.action: Retrieve required, expected, optional, and conditional evidence expectations applicable to the pipeline context.
Mark the required evidence requirement as satisfied.
Mark the applicable evidence requirement as missing and preserve the gap for downstream assessment and recommendation logic.
Do not automatically assign a negative evidence value solely because required evidence is absent.

evidenceConfidenceRules.action: Initialize evidence confidence from evidence strength, relevance, source quality, freshness, corroboration, and contradiction status.
Restrict the maximum confidence assigned to the affected evidence conclusion.
Restrict evidence confidence according to the configured maximum confidence for unverified evidence.
Classify the evidence as qualified evidence for downstream PADF assessment use.
Classify the evidence as unqualified for direct downstream assessment use while retaining it as contextual information.

evidenceEvaluationSummaryRules.action: Create a normalized evidence evaluation record containing evidence identity, source, relevance, quality, freshness, strength, corroboration, contradiction, completeness, and confidence attributes.
Record the rule execution chain and evidence references supporting the evaluation result.
Make the qualified evidence available to downstream PADF dimension assessment rules.
Retain unqualified evidence for contextual awareness, evidence-gap analysis, and future reassessment without allowing it to directly drive deterministic dimension scoring.

phaseCompletionRules.action: Mark Phase 3 evidence evaluation as completed and release qualified evidence to the downstream PADF assessment layer.
Block downstream evidence-driven assessment until the required evaluation foundation is available.

phaseDefinition.phaseName: PADF Dimension Scoring & Health Calculation Layer
phaseDefinition.purpose: Convert qualified and evaluated pipeline evidence into normalized PADF dimension scores, dimension health states, and dimension-level confidence inputs for downstream pipeline health, risk, and winning strategy calculations.

principles.description: PADF dimension scores must be derived from evaluated evidence rather than unsupported assumptions or subjective judgment.
Each PADF dimension must be evaluated according to its own definition, evidence expectations, scoring behavior, and applicable revenue motion and industry configuration.
Only evidence that has passed the Phase 3 evidence qualification process may directly contribute to deterministic dimension scoring.
Evidence contribution must reflect evidence strength, relevance, confidence, freshness, and corroboration rather than treating all evidence as equally valuable.
Evidence may contribute positively, negatively, or neutrally to a dimension depending on the condition demonstrated by the evidence.
Missing evidence must reduce assessment confidence or evidence completeness but must not automatically be interpreted as negative evidence.
Dimension scoring behavior must be determined by the applicable Pipeline Industry Configuration rather than hard-coded industry assumptions.
The same PADF dimension may require different evidence weighting, thresholds, or scoring behavior depending on the active revenue motion family.
Industry-specific configuration may modify dimension evidence expectations, scoring weights, thresholds, and interpretation without changing the universal PADF framework.
The engine must distinguish between a dimension score and confidence in that score so that a numerically precise score is not mistaken for high-confidence evidence.
Every dimension score must be traceable to the evidence objects, evidence contributions, configuration rules, and calculation rules that produced it.
Dimension scores must be calculated in a way that permits later comparison with prior assessment snapshots and identification of score evolution.

processingSequence: Retrieve qualified evidence mapped to each dimension

dimensionResolutionRules.action: Retrieve the PADF dimensions applicable to the active pipeline assessment context.
Apply the PADF dimension behavior configured for the resolved revenue motion family.
Apply applicable industry-specific PADF dimension configuration using the configured inheritance and override model.
Exclude the dimension from active score calculation while preserving the applicability decision in the assessment record.

dimensionEvaluationStates.description: The dimension has not yet been evaluated.
The dimension is applicable but insufficient qualified evidence exists to support a reliable score.
The dimension has sufficient evidence to produce a score, but confidence is limited.
The dimension has sufficient qualified evidence and an interpretable score.
The dimension is not applicable to the active pipeline context.

evidenceContributionRules.action: Include qualified evidence mapped to the active PADF dimension in the dimension scoring set.
Exclude context-only evidence from deterministic dimension score contribution.
Determine whether the evidence contributes positively, negatively, or neutrally to the active PADF dimension.
Assign a positive contribution to the dimension score according to the configured evidence contribution weight.
Assign a negative contribution to the dimension score according to the configured evidence contribution weight.
Retain the evidence for contextual interpretation without materially increasing or decreasing the dimension score.
Apply the evidence-strength weighting defined by the applicable evidence configuration.
Apply the evaluated evidence confidence as a contribution reliability factor.
Apply the configured freshness adjustment to the evidence contribution.
Apply the configured corroboration adjustment to the evidence contribution.
Reduce or cap the contribution of evidence affected by unresolved contradiction according to the applicable configuration.
Calculate the normalized contribution of the evidence item to the active PADF dimension using configured evidence weighting factors.

dimensionScoreCalculationRules.action: Initialize the dimension score calculation using the applicable PADF dimension configuration.
Retrieve the configured scoring model, scale, weight, thresholds, and aggregation behavior for the active PADF dimension.
Aggregate normalized positive evidence contributions for the active PADF dimension.
Aggregate normalized negative evidence contributions for the active PADF dimension.
Calculate net dimension evidence by combining positive and negative evidence contributions.
Apply the configured PADF dimension weight to the normalized dimension result.
Normalize the calculated PADF dimension result to the scoring scale defined by the applicable configuration.
Set the dimension score to the configured minimum value.
Set the dimension score to the configured maximum value.
Calculate the proportion of applicable expected evidence represented by qualified evidence for the active dimension.
Aggregate evidence strength across the dimension's qualified evidence set using the configured aggregation method.
Create a dimension evaluation record containing dimension identity, score, evidence coverage, evidence strength, evidence references, calculation inputs, and rule trace.
Mark the dimension as assessed when evidence coverage satisfies the configured minimum assessment threshold.
Mark the dimension as insufficiently evidenced and prevent the dimension score from being interpreted as high-confidence.

dimensionHealthClassificationRules.action: Initialize health classification processing for the evaluated PADF dimension.
Retrieve applicable dimension health thresholds from Pipeline Industry Configuration using inheritance and override resolution.
Classify the dimension as moderate health.
Prevent the dimension from being classified as healthy when evidence coverage is insufficient.
Create dimension health record containing score, health state, evidence coverage, and assessment confidence inputs.

dimensionConfidenceRules.action: Initialize confidence calculation for the dimension assessment.
Calculate confidence contribution from evidence coverage completeness.
Calculate confidence contribution from evidence strength and quality.
Adjust dimension confidence according to evidence freshness.
Calculate normalized confidence score for the PADF dimension assessment.

missingEvidenceImpactRules.action: Identify missing evidence required for complete PADF dimension evaluation.
Calculate the impact of missing evidence on dimension confidence and assessment completeness.
Prevent missing evidence from directly reducing dimension score unless explicitly configured as negative evidence.

dimensionDependencyRules.action: Resolve dependency relationships between PADF dimensions.
Apply configured dependency impact adjustments when one PADF dimension materially influences another.

pipelineHealthAggregationPreparationRule.action: Prepare all dimension health records as input dataset for downstream pipeline health calculation.
Preserve all dimension scores, evidence references, confidence levels, and calculation traces for downstream reasoning.

phaseCompletionRules.action: Mark Phase 4 PADF Dimension Scoring & Health Calculation Layer as completed.

phaseDefinition.purpose: Evaluate interactions among PADF dimensions and apply configured dependency, reinforcement, contradiction, constraint, risk-compounding, and cross-dimensional adjustment logic to produce a more holistic pipeline assessment.

crossDimensionalReasoningPrinciples.description: Pipeline assessment must consider meaningful interactions among PADF dimensions rather than treating each dimension as an independent and isolated score.
Cross-dimensional relationships must be evaluated only when explicitly defined by the applicable Pipeline Industry Configuration or evidence knowledge base.
A materially dependent dimension must not be treated as fully effective when its prerequisite dimension is materially weak.
Independent positive dimensions may reinforce one another when their configured relationship indicates that their combined strength materially improves pipeline health.
Conflicting dimension states must be explicitly identified rather than hidden through averaging.
A critical weak dimension may constrain the effective value of otherwise strong dimensions when the applicable configuration defines such a constraint.
Multiple individually moderate weaknesses may create materially greater pipeline risk when they interact in a configured risk-compounding pattern.
Cross-dimensional reasoning must remain bounded by the evidence quality and confidence of the underlying dimension assessments.
The same evidence must not create multiple independent scoring effects unless the configuration explicitly permits such reuse.
Cross-dimensional adjustments must remain within configured minimum and maximum adjustment limits.
Every cross-dimensional adjustment must identify the triggering dimensions, relationship, rule, adjustment magnitude, and evidence basis.
Original Phase 4 dimension scores must be preserved and must never be overwritten by cross-dimensional adjustments.
Cross-dimensional adjustments must account for the confidence of the dimensions participating in the relationship.
Cross-dimensional relationships and adjustment behavior must follow the resolved revenue motion and industry configuration.

crossDimensionalContextResolutionRules.action: Initialize cross-dimensional reasoning using the completed Phase 4 PADF dimension assessment dataset.
Retrieve applicable cross-dimensional relationship configurations using universal baseline, revenue motion override, and industry override precedence.
Build the active set of configured dimension relationships applicable to the pipeline.
Exclude the relationship from active cross-dimensional reasoning while preserving the applicability decision.

dimensionDependencyRules.action: Identify the prerequisite and dependent PADF dimensions in the configured dependency relationship.
Evaluate the health and confidence of the prerequisite dimension.
Apply the configured dependency constraint to the dependent dimension without changing its original Phase 4 score.
Apply configured positive dependency support to the dependent dimension.

dimensionReinforcementRules.action: Identify PADF dimensions configured as mutually reinforcing.
Evaluate whether the participating dimensions satisfy the configured score, health, and confidence thresholds for reinforcement.
Apply the configured positive cross-dimensional reinforcement adjustment.
Reduce or suppress positive reinforcement when one or more participating dimensions have low confidence.

dimensionContradictionRules.action: Identify configured contradictions among PADF dimensions.
Compare the health, score, evidence coverage, and confidence of the contradictory dimensions.
Create a material cross-dimensional contradiction signal for downstream risk and winability assessment.
Apply the configured negative cross-dimensional adjustment while preserving the original dimension scores.
Increase assessment uncertainty and preserve the contradiction as an explicit unresolved assessment signal.

dimensionConstraintRules.action: Identify dimensions configured as critical constraints on other dimensions or on the pipeline assessment.
Evaluate whether the constrained dimension satisfies the configured critical threshold.
Apply the configured constraint adjustment and create a critical constraint signal.
Record the constraining dimension, constrained dimension, triggering threshold, and adjustment applied.

riskCompoundingRules.action: Identify configured combinations of weak, deteriorating, or uncertain PADF dimensions that may create compound pipeline risk.
Evaluate the participating dimension health states, confidence levels, evidence coverage, and configured severity conditions.
Create a compound risk signal representing the combined effect of the participating dimensions.
Apply the configured compound-risk adjustment to the cross-dimensional assessment state.
Prevent duplicate adjustment for the same underlying dimension weakness or evidence pattern.

crossDimensionalAssessmentAdjustmentRule.action: Aggregate applicable positive and negative cross-dimensional adjustment events.
Apply configured precedence when multiple cross-dimensional adjustments affect the same dimension or assessment attribute.
Cap the aggregate cross-dimensional adjustment at the configured minimum or maximum adjustment boundary.
Calculate an adjusted dimension assessment value while preserving the original Phase 4 score.
Preserve the original Phase 4 dimension score as the immutable base score and store the adjusted value separately.
Determine whether cross-dimensional adjustments change the applicable dimension health classification.
Adjust dimension confidence when cross-dimensional contradiction, evidence insufficiency, or unresolved dependency materially increases uncertainty.
Create a complete trace of all cross-dimensional relationships, triggered rules, participating dimensions, adjustments, constraints, and uncertainty signals.

assessmentConsistencyRules.action: Check for materially inconsistent combinations of dimension score, health state, evidence coverage, and confidence.
Create an assessment consistency warning without automatically changing the underlying dimension score.
Create an assessment consistency warning when confidence materially conflicts with evidence coverage or quality.

crossDimensionalOutputRules.action: Create the cross-dimensional assessment record containing original dimension scores, adjusted dimension scores, relationship signals, constraints, reinforcement effects, contradiction signals, compound risks, and confidence adjustments.
Store original Phase 4 values and Phase 5 adjusted values as separate attributes for auditability and historical comparison.
Prepare the cross-dimensional assessment dataset for downstream pipeline health, winability, risk, and strategy calculation.

phaseCompletionRules.action: Mark Phase 5 Cross-Dimensional Reasoning & Adjustment Layer as completed.

phaseDefinition.purpose: Transform the adjusted PADF dimension assessment and cross-dimensional reasoning outputs into an overall pipeline health assessment, winability assessment, confidence-adjusted winability, forecast reliability, pipeline maturity, and assessment status.
scope: Downstream risk and winning strategy input preparation
excludedFromPhase: Closed Won or Closed Lost determination

winabilityOutputContractV1_1.baseWinability: Calculated in Rules Phase 6 using the existing approved methodology and existing PADF/cross-dimensional inputs.
winabilityOutputContractV1_1.riskAdjustedWinability: Not finalized in Phase 6; calculated in Rules Phase 7 using base winability and authoritative risk outputs.
winabilityOutputContractV1_1.swotInfluence: SWOT factor scores must not be introduced as a new composite or direct replacement for the existing winability calculation.

pipelineHealthCalculationRules.action: Initialize pipeline-level health calculation using the adjusted PADF assessment dataset.
Resolve applicable PADF dimension weights using universal baseline, revenue motion override, and industry override precedence.
Calculate each PADF dimension's weighted contribution to overall pipeline health using the adjusted dimension assessment.
Calculate the normalized base pipeline health score from weighted PADF dimension contributions.
Apply eligible Phase 5 cross-dimensional health adjustments to the base pipeline health score.
Apply the configured pipeline-level health constraint associated with a critical PADF dimension.
Constrain the final pipeline health score to the configured minimum and maximum boundaries.

winabilityCalculationRules.action: Resolve the configured contribution of PADF dimensions and cross-dimensional signals to pipeline winability.
Calculate the normalized base winability score using adjusted PADF dimension scores and applicable winability weights.
Apply eligible positive reinforcement and supportive dependency effects to the winability calculation.
Apply eligible contradiction, constraint, dependency failure, and compound-risk effects to the winability calculation.
Apply the configured maximum winability constraint when a fatal or near-fatal pipeline condition is present.
Calculate the raw pipeline winability score after applicable cross-dimensional adjustments and constraints.
Constrain raw winability to the configured minimum and maximum boundaries.

confidenceAdjustedWinabilityRules.action: Calculate aggregate assessment confidence from PADF dimension confidence, evidence coverage, evidence quality, freshness, and unresolved uncertainty.
Convert aggregate assessment confidence into the configured winability confidence adjustment factor.
Calculate confidence-adjusted winability using raw winability and the configured confidence treatment.
Prevent low assessment confidence from producing an unjustifiably high confidence-adjusted winability result.

winabilityClassificationRules.action: Classify the pipeline as high winability.
Classify the pipeline as moderate winability.
Classify the pipeline as low winability.
Flag winability as uncertain when the available evidence is insufficient to support a reliable probability assessment.

pipelineHealthClassificationRules.action: Classify the pipeline as at risk.
Prevent the pipeline from being classified above the configured critical-health ceiling.

pipelineMaturityRules.action: Evaluate evidence completeness, stakeholder coverage, decision-process clarity, commercial readiness, technical readiness, and execution readiness to determine pipeline maturity.
Classify the pipeline as early stage.

forecastReliabilityRules.action: Calculate forecast reliability from evidence confidence, evidence freshness, dimension coverage, stakeholder evidence, decision-process evidence, and unresolved contradictions.
Reduce forecast reliability when critical pipeline evidence has exceeded its configured freshness window.
Reduce forecast reliability when material cross-dimensional contradictions remain unresolved.

pipelineUncertaintyRules.action: Calculate pipeline-level uncertainty from evidence gaps, low-confidence dimensions, unresolved contradictions, stale evidence, and missing critical stakeholder or decision evidence.
Classify pipeline assessment uncertainty as low.
Classify pipeline assessment uncertainty as moderate.
Classify pipeline assessment uncertainty as high.

pipelineAssessmentConsistencyRules.action: Check whether pipeline health, winability, confidence, and critical constraint states are materially inconsistent.
Flag a material health-winability mismatch for downstream reasoning.
Flag a material health-winability mismatch for downstream reasoning.
Flag high nominal winability as unreliable when forecast reliability is low.

pipelineAssessmentOutputRules.action: Create the consolidated pipeline assessment result.
Preserve the calculation lineage from inherited qualification data through evidence evaluation, PADF scoring, cross-dimensional adjustment, health calculation, and winability calculation.
Prepare critical constraints, compound-risk signals, contradictions, weak dimensions, and uncertainty signals for downstream risk intelligence.
Prepare the pipeline health, winability, maturity, uncertainty, constraint, and dimension-gap outputs for downstream winning strategy reasoning.

phaseCompletionRules.action: Mark Phase 6 Winability & Pipeline Health Calculation Layer as completed.

phaseDefinition.phaseName: Risk Detection & Risk Aggregation Rule Layer
phaseDefinition.purpose: Detect, classify, evaluate, prioritize, correlate, and aggregate risks that may reduce the probability of winning a qualified pipeline.

riskAdjustedWinabilityContractV1_1.riskAdjustedWinabilityOutput: Calculated after authoritative risk evaluation using existing risk impact and ceiling rules.

riskDetectionRules.action: Initialize pipeline risk detection using evidence, PADF dimension assessments, cross-dimensional signals, pipeline health, winability, uncertainty, and forecast reliability.
Resolve applicable risk rules using universal baseline, revenue motion family overrides, and industry-specific overrides.
Scan evaluated evidence for explicit and implicit risk signals defined in the applicable risk configuration.
Identify risk signals generated by weak, declining, incomplete, or critically constrained PADF dimensions.
Identify risk signals generated by contradictions, dependencies, reinforcing weaknesses, and negative cross-dimensional interactions.
Identify pipeline-level risks derived from low winability, poor health, low maturity, low forecast reliability, high uncertainty, and critical constraints.
Deduplicate risk signals referring to the same underlying risk condition while preserving all supporting evidence references.

riskClassificationRules.action: Classify each detected risk into the applicable risk domain.
Classify each risk according to its underlying risk mechanism.
Classify the risk as a critical pipeline risk.

riskSeverityRules.action: Estimate the probability that each detected risk will materially affect pipeline progression or winability using evidence strength, signal recurrence, dimension weakness, and cross-dimensional reinforcement.
Estimate the potential impact of each risk on pipeline winability, deal progression, commercial outcome, timing, or execution.
Calculate risk severity from risk probability, risk impact, criticality, and configured risk rules.
Calculate risk urgency using severity, decision timing, pipeline stage timing, evidence freshness, and proximity to irreversible customer decisions.
Calculate overall risk exposure using probability, impact, severity, urgency, and configured risk exposure weights.

compoundRiskRules.action: Identify groups of risks whose combined effect is materially greater than the individual risks considered separately.
Identify reinforcing risks where weakness in one condition increases the probability or impact of another risk.
Identify risk clusters spanning multiple PADF dimensions.
Apply the configured compound-risk multiplier to the aggregate exposure of materially reinforcing or cross-dimensional risk clusters.

riskCorrelationRules.action: Map each material risk to the PADF dimensions it weakens or constrains.
Determine the relationship between material risks and the current pipeline winability assessment.
Identify the risk as a winability-blocking risk.
Identify the risk as materially constraining pipeline health.

riskPriorityRules.action: Assign the highest risk priority to critical risks.
Assign high priority to risks with high aggregate exposure.
Assign medium priority to risks with moderate aggregate exposure.
Assign low priority to risks with low aggregate exposure.
Elevate risk priority when a material risk requires immediate attention because the customer decision or pipeline milestone is imminent.

aggregateRiskRules.action: Calculate aggregate pipeline risk exposure from material individual risks.
Apply compound-risk adjustments to aggregate pipeline risk exposure.
Apply the configured critical-risk override to aggregate pipeline risk.
Constrain aggregate pipeline risk score to the configured minimum and maximum boundaries.

riskConcentrationRules.action: Calculate the concentration of material risks across PADF dimensions, risk domains, and stakeholder or decision dependencies.
Identify a single stakeholder, decision condition, technical dependency, commercial condition, or other factor whose failure could materially jeopardize the pipeline.
Identify concentrated risk exposure across multiple PADF dimensions.

riskPostureRules.action: Classify overall pipeline risk posture as low.
Classify overall pipeline risk posture as moderate.
Classify overall pipeline risk posture as high.
Classify pipeline risk posture as critical when at least one configured critical win-blocking risk remains unresolved.

riskWinabilityImpactRules.action: Calculate the aggregate estimated impact of identified risks on current pipeline winability.
Apply the configured maximum winability ceiling when a material risk is identified as directly blocking the ability to win.
Flag the pipeline as having a material risk-adjusted winability gap.

riskOutputRules.action: Create the consolidated pipeline risk register containing detected risks, domains, evidence, severity, probability, impact, urgency, exposure, priority, affected PADF dimensions, and winability impact.
Preserve traceability from every material risk to its supporting evidence, PADF dimension, cross-dimensional signal, and upstream assessment result.
Prepare prioritized risks, critical constraints, risk clusters, single points of failure, risk-adjusted winability impact, and risk posture for the downstream winning strategy engine.

phaseCompletionRules.action: Mark Phase 7 Risk Detection & Risk Aggregation Rule Layer as completed.

phaseDefinition.purpose: Convert pipeline assessment findings, evidence gaps, dimension weaknesses, risks, winability constraints, revenue motion characteristics, and industry context into prioritized, evidence-grounded winning strategies and actionable recommendations.
excludedFromPhase: Automatic win probability override without evidence
Automatic closure of risks without new evidence

swotIntegrationHandoffV1_1.engineOwnership: Existing Winning Strategy engine remains authoritative. The adapter translates and validates inputs but does not replace recommendation generation or action prioritization.

strategyInitializationRules.action: Initialize the winning strategy engine using current pipeline assessment, PADF dimension results, evidence status, risk register, winability, pipeline health, revenue motion, industry context, and customer decision context.
Resolve applicable winning strategy patterns using universal baseline, revenue motion family overrides, and industry-specific overrides.

Resolve the strategic context required for recommendation generation, including revenue motion, industry, customer situation, buying process, competitive environment, commercial model, timeline, and pipeline stage.

strategicGapRules.action: Identify the highest-impact condition currently preventing or limiting the pipeline from progressing toward a win.
Identify additional material gaps that materially constrain winability but are not the primary winning gap.
Identify evidence gaps that prevent reliable strategic decisions or materially reduce confidence in pipeline winability.
Identify the condition creating the material gap between current potential winability and risk-adjusted winability.

winningObjectiveRules.action: Define the primary strategic objective required to materially improve the pipeline's probability of winning.
Define a risk mitigation objective for every critical risk that directly threatens the ability to win.
Define evidence acquisition objectives required to resolve material uncertainty.

strategyGenerationRules.action: Generate a primary winning strategy aligned with the pipeline's revenue motion, industry context, customer decision process, primary gap, and risk profile.
Generate strategies specifically designed to reduce or neutralize material and critical risks.
Generate evidence acquisition strategies for material evidence gaps that affect strategic confidence or winability.
Generate a stakeholder strategy addressing missing, weak, misaligned, or insufficiently engaged decision stakeholders.
Generate a competitive strategy based on known competitor position, customer decision criteria, differentiation gaps, incumbent position, and competitive evidence.
Generate a value strategy designed to strengthen customer-perceived business value, economic justification, and differentiation.
Generate a commercial strategy addressing budget, pricing, procurement, contracting, commercial structure, and approval barriers.
Generate a decision process strategy addressing buying process clarity, decision criteria, approval path, decision authority, and next decision milestone.
Generate a technical strategy addressing solution fit, architecture, integration, proof, feasibility, implementation, and technical objections.
Generate a timing strategy addressing customer urgency, decision deadlines, procurement timing, implementation milestones, and competitive timing.

strategicMoveRules.action: Convert the winning strategy into discrete strategic moves that can be executed and subsequently evidenced.
Define the intended outcome of each strategic move in measurable or evidence-verifiable terms.
Define the evidence that should confirm successful completion or effectiveness of each strategic move.

recommendationPrioritizationRules.action: Estimate the expected impact of each recommendation on winability, pipeline health, risk reduction, evidence confidence, or deal progression.
Calculate recommendation urgency based on risk severity, customer decision timing, pipeline stage, and consequence of delay.
Estimate the feasibility of executing each recommendation using available resources, customer access, timing, authority, technical capability, and organizational constraints.
Calculate recommendation priority using expected impact, urgency, feasibility, risk reduction, and strategic importance.

recommendationDependencyRules.action: Identify dependencies between recommendations, including prerequisite evidence, stakeholder access, technical validation, commercial approval, and customer decision milestones.
Sequence recommendations according to prerequisite dependencies, urgency, customer decision timing, and expected strategic impact.

expectedImpactRules.action: Estimate the potential contribution of each recommendation to improving pipeline winability if the underlying condition is successfully changed and subsequently evidenced.
Estimate the potential reduction in risk exposure if the recommendation succeeds.
Estimate the potential improvement in pipeline health resulting from successful execution of material recommendations.
Adjust expected impact confidence according to evidence strength, evidence completeness, dependency uncertainty, and execution uncertainty.

strategyConfidenceRules.action: Calculate confidence in the strategy using the quality, completeness, freshness, and directness of supporting evidence.
Calculate confidence that the recommended strategy can realistically be executed within the current pipeline context.
Calculate overall strategy confidence using evidence confidence, execution confidence, contextual fit, and uncertainty.

strategyValidationRules.action: Validate that every material strategy and recommendation is grounded in available evidence, configured industry intelligence, risk findings, or explicitly identified evidence gaps.
Validate that recommendations do not materially contradict the current PADF assessment, risk assessment, revenue motion configuration, or industry context.
Validate that recommendations represent actionable strategic moves rather than generic advice or unsupported statements.
Reject recommendations that rely on fabricated customer facts, competitor facts, stakeholder facts, commercial facts, or other unsupported information.

executiveRecommendationRules.action: Create a concise primary executive recommendation describing the most important strategic move required to improve the probability of winning.
Create the prioritized set of recommendations required to execute the winning strategy.
Create explicit strategic responses for every critical risk that remains unresolved.
Create prioritized recommendations for obtaining the evidence required to reduce material uncertainty.

strategyOutcomeRules.action: Create the consolidated winning strategy plan containing strategic objective, primary strategy, strategic moves, recommendation priorities, dependencies, risks addressed, evidence required, and expected impact.
Prepare structured execution tracking inputs so that future pipeline assessments can determine whether recommended strategic moves were executed and whether supporting evidence changed.
Prepare the structured inputs required for future pipeline reassessment, including prior risks, recommendations, expected impacts, execution status, and evidence changes.

phaseCompletionRules.action: Mark Phase 8 Winning Strategy & Recommendation Decision Layer as completed.

phaseDefinition.purpose: Govern the longitudinal evolution of a qualified pipeline across assessment cycles by preserving assessment history, detecting material changes, measuring trajectory, evaluating recommendation execution and effectiveness, identifying reassessment triggers, and governing pipeline lifecycle transitions.
excludedFromPhase: Automatic opportunity closure without authoritative evidence
Retroactive alteration of previous assessment results

swotLifecycleIntegrationV1_1.historyPolicy: Preserve immutable prior assessment snapshots; reassessment creates a new governed revision or cycle.

assessmentCycleInitializationRules.action: Initialize a new assessment cycle for the current pipeline assessment event.
Assign a unique assessment cycle identifier and preserve the assessment timestamp.
Identify the immediately preceding valid assessment snapshot for the same pipeline when one exists.
Establish the comparison context between the current assessment and the immediately preceding valid assessment.

assessmentSnapshotRules.action: Create an immutable assessment snapshot containing the current assessment state, evidence state, PADF scores, pipeline health, winability, risks, strategies, and recommendations.
Preserve the evidence inputs, configuration context, scoring inputs, and reasoning inputs used to produce the assessment.
Mark the assessment snapshot as immutable so subsequent assessments cannot overwrite historical results.

changeDetectionRules.action: Compare current evidence against the previous assessment and identify newly added, removed, updated, expired, contradicted, or strengthened evidence.
Detect material changes in customer situation, buying process, stakeholders, competition, commercial conditions, timing, scope, or implementation context.
Compare current PADF dimension results against the previous assessment and identify material positive or negative changes.
Compare current winability against previous winability and classify the change as improved, deteriorated, stable, or indeterminate.
Compare current pipeline health against previous pipeline health and classify the change as improved, deteriorated, stable, or indeterminate.
Compare current risks against previous risks and identify newly emerged, escalated, reduced, resolved, persistent, or reactivated risks.

trajectoryAnalysisRules.action: Analyze the historical direction and momentum of pipeline winability across available assessment cycles.
Analyze the historical direction and momentum of pipeline health across available assessment cycles.
Analyze whether the pipeline risk profile is improving, deteriorating, stable, or repeatedly re-emerging.
Track the trajectory of each PADF dimension and identify persistent strengths, persistent weaknesses, improving dimensions, and deteriorating dimensions.
Determine overall pipeline momentum using winability trajectory, health trajectory, risk trajectory, evidence progression, and material pipeline changes.

recommendationExecutionRules.action: Determine the execution status of recommendations generated in the previous assessment cycle.
Classify each recommendation as not started, in progress, completed, partially completed, blocked, abandoned, or unverifiable.
Determine whether sufficient evidence exists to evaluate the outcome of executed recommendations.
Evaluate whether executed recommendations produced the intended evidence change, risk reduction, dimension improvement, health improvement, winability improvement, or progression.
Identify recommendations or strategic approaches that were executed but failed to produce the intended improvement.
Identify recommendations or strategic approaches that produced measurable positive changes.

reassessmentTriggerRules.action: Trigger a reassessment when material new, changed, contradicted, expired, or strengthened evidence could affect the pipeline assessment.
Trigger a reassessment when a material risk emerges, escalates, is resolved, or reactivates.
Trigger reassessment when a material change occurs in customer situation, buying process, stakeholders, competition, commercial conditions, timing, scope, or implementation context.
Trigger reassessment when pipeline winability demonstrates material deterioration.
Trigger reassessment when pipeline health demonstrates material deterioration.
Trigger reassessment when the pipeline shows insufficient progression over the configured assessment period.
Trigger reassessment when the pipeline reaches its configured assessment review interval.
Trigger reassessment when material winning strategies or recommendations fail to produce their intended outcomes.

lifecycleGovernanceRules.action: Determine the current pipeline lifecycle state using pipeline stage, progression, evidence status, winability, health, risks, customer decision status, and closure signals.
Determine whether the pipeline has materially progressed toward the customer decision or commercial close milestone.
Classify the pipeline as stagnating when insufficient meaningful progression occurs despite continued pipeline existence.
Classify the pipeline as materially deteriorating when both winability and pipeline health demonstrate sustained deterioration.
Classify the pipeline as recovering when winability and pipeline health materially improve following a prior weak or deteriorating state.

closureGovernanceRules.action: Recognize an authoritative Closed Won signal and prepare the pipeline for Closed Won lifecycle transition.
Recognize an authoritative Closed Lost signal and prepare the pipeline for Closed Lost lifecycle transition.
Transition the pipeline lifecycle state to Closed Won while preserving the complete historical assessment trajectory and final evidence state.
Transition the pipeline lifecycle state to Closed Lost while preserving the complete historical assessment trajectory and final evidence state.
Require an evidence-supported loss reason or explicitly mark the loss reason as unavailable or unverified.

reactivationGovernanceRules.action: Detect whether new authoritative evidence indicates that a previously inactive or closed-lost pipeline has re-entered an active buying process.
Require sufficient new evidence of customer intent, decision activity, engagement, or commercial progression before reactivation.
Allow the pipeline to return to an active lifecycle state and require a new assessment cycle using current evidence.

executiveEscalationRules.action: Trigger executive review when pipeline winability and health materially deteriorate.
Trigger executive review when critical risks remain unresolved across multiple assessment cycles.
Trigger executive review when the pipeline remains materially stagnant beyond the configured tolerance period.

evolutionSummaryRules.action: Generate a longitudinal summary describing what changed, why it changed, whether the pipeline improved or deteriorated, which risks changed, and whether previous recommendations were effective.
Generate an executive-level assessment of pipeline trajectory, momentum, strategic effectiveness, remaining risks, and required management attention.

phaseCompletionRules.action: Mark Phase 9 Pipeline Evolution & Lifecycle Governance Layer as completed.

phaseDefinition.purpose: Coordinate the complete Pipeline Assessment rule execution lifecycle, enforce phase dependencies and execution integrity, validate outputs, maintain auditability, govern exceptions, preserve assessment traceability, and ensure that the final pipeline assessment is complete, explainable, reproducible, and governance compliant.
excludedFromPhase: Fabrication or inference of unavailable evidence as factual evidence
Automatic override of authoritative user or system data without governance authorization

swotAuditIntegrationV1_1.mandatoryLineage: Evidence instance -> KB mapping -> canonical SWOT factor -> factor evaluation -> TOWS -> risk/winability -> strategy adapter -> existing strategy output -> action and lifecycle history.

orchestrationRules.action: Initialize the Pipeline Assessment execution context and assign a unique assessment execution identifier.
Resolve the applicable Pipeline Industry Configuration, Evidence Knowledge Base, Assessment Rules version, revenue motion, industry configuration, and assessment context.
Validate that all required configuration assets and compatible versions are available before assessment execution begins.
Create the ordered execution plan covering Phases 2 through 9 and required validation checkpoints.
Enforce the configured dependency order so that downstream phases cannot execute before their required upstream outputs are available and valid.
Execute required assessment phases according to the execution plan and dependency requirements.

inputValidationRules.action: Validate the inherited pipeline and qualification data required from the Opportunity Qualification module.
Validate that the pipeline has a valid identity and can be uniquely associated with the assessment context.
Validate the structure, provenance, recency, status, and usability of available pipeline assessment evidence.
Determine whether required inputs are missing and classify missing inputs according to their impact on assessment reliability.
Block downstream assessment execution when critical inputs are invalid or unavailable.

phaseExecutionGovernanceRules.action: Validate the entry conditions, required inputs, upstream outputs, and configuration dependencies before executing each phase.
Execute the applicable phase rules using the resolved configuration and current assessment context.
Validate that the phase generated all required outputs and that outputs conform to the expected structure and semantic requirements.
Prevent transition to downstream phases when the current phase output is invalid or incomplete.
Authorize transition to the next phase in the execution plan.

crossPhaseConsistencyRules.action: Validate that customer, pipeline, revenue motion, industry, and assessment context remain consistent across all executed phases.
Validate that PADF dimension results used by downstream calculations are internally consistent and traceable to their evidence inputs.
Validate that the final winability result is consistent with the applicable dimension scores, cross-dimensional adjustments, and calculation rules.
Validate that detected risks are traceable to evidence and remain consistent with pipeline health and winability results.
Validate that winning strategies and recommendations are logically connected to the current assessment, identified risks, weak dimensions, and improvement opportunities.

traceabilityRules.action: Ensure material assessment conclusions can be traced back to identifiable evidence objects and evidence sources.
Ensure material dimension scores and health calculations can be traced to the evidence and rules that generated them.
Ensure material risks can be traced to their triggering evidence and applicable risk rules.
Ensure each material recommendation can be traced to the relevant weakness, risk, evidence gap, strategic objective, or improvement opportunity.
Preserve structured reasoning references sufficient to explain how evidence and rule outputs contributed to assessment conclusions and recommendations.

auditRules.action: Create an audit record containing the assessment execution identifier, timestamp, pipeline identifier, configuration versions, and execution context.
Record material rule execution events including rule identifier, execution status, input references, output references, timestamp, and exception status.
Record the versions of all configuration and knowledge assets used during the assessment.
Preserve the complete execution trail required to reproduce and audit the assessment result.

exceptionHandlingRules.action: Create an execution exception and identify the affected rule, phase, inputs, and downstream dependencies.
Classify the exception as recoverable, non-recoverable, data-related, configuration-related, rule-related, system-related, or governance-related.
Allow controlled retry of the affected rule or phase within the configured retry policy.
Stop affected downstream execution and escalate the failure for human or system-level resolution.

insufficientEvidenceGovernanceRules.action: Classify evidence sufficiency as sufficient, partially sufficient, insufficient, or materially insufficient for the intended assessment confidence.
Restrict assessment confidence and explicitly expose material evidence limitations rather than treating unavailable information as negative or positive evidence.
Generate a governance signal identifying the critical evidence gaps that limit assessment reliability.

conflictGovernanceRules.action: Detect material contradictions between evidence objects, customer statements, stakeholder inputs, system data, or assessment observations.
Resolve conflicting evidence according to evidence provenance, authority, recency, directness, and reliability rules without silently discarding conflicting information.
Expose the unresolved conflict as an assessment limitation and prevent unsupported certainty.

humanReviewRules.action: Determine whether human review is required based on critical risks, material evidence conflicts, insufficient evidence, execution exceptions, major strategic recommendations, or governance thresholds.
Route the assessment to the designated human reviewer before final publication.
Record the reviewer decision, review timestamp, decision rationale, approved changes, rejected changes, and unresolved issues.

assessmentFinalizationRules.action: Validate that all required assessment outputs from Phases 2 through 9 have been successfully generated or explicitly marked as unavailable, restricted, or not applicable.
Validate audit trail, traceability, evidence sufficiency, conflict handling, exception handling, and human review requirements.
Authorize the current assessment snapshot for finalization.
Finalize the current assessment snapshot and prevent uncontrolled modification of the finalized result.
Publish the finalized Pipeline Assessment result to authorized downstream RevOS components and users.

postAssessmentGovernanceRules.action: Register the finalized assessment snapshot in the pipeline assessment history.
Make the finalized assessment snapshot available as the historical baseline for future Pipeline Assessment cycles.
Create the final governance completion record containing execution status, validation status, exception status, review status, audit status, and publication status.

phaseCompletionRules.action: Mark Phase 10 Orchestration, Audit & Governance Integration Layer as completed and mark the current Pipeline Assessment execution as governance complete.

integrationMetadata.governingPrinciple: Rules orchestrate deterministic execution and integration; KB owns evidence objects and approved mappings; Industry Configuration owns SWOT factor definitions, factor evaluation criteria and TOWS; existing Rules Phase 7 Risk Intelligence and Phase 8 Winning Strategy remain authoritative.
integrationMetadata.phaseNamespacePolicy: All new cross-asset references must use fully qualified asset, phase and component names. Never use an unqualified phase number across assets.
integrationMetadata.ruleIdentifierPolicy: New rules use globally distinct RSW-prefixed IDs and qualifiedRuleId. Existing legacy ruleId values remain unchanged; ambiguous legacy dependencies must not be resolved arbitrarily.
integrationMetadata.generationNote: Draft generated in Stage 5. Crosswalk entries not authoritatively established by source assets remain unresolved and require explicit approval.

ownershipAndBoundaries.rulesEngine: Owns runtime orchestration, deterministic validation, execution dependencies, integration adapters, lifecycle coordination and audit integration.
ownershipAndBoundaries.evidenceKnowledgeBase: Owns reusable evidence definitions, approved evidence-to-SWOT mapping records, mapping strength and evidence intelligence contracts.
ownershipAndBoundaries.industryConfiguration: Owns contextual factor definitions, factor evaluation criteria, SWOT taxonomy, evidence-gap governance, TOWS definitions and evolution governance.
ownershipAndBoundaries.riskIntelligence: Existing Rules Phase 7 remains authoritative for runtime risk detection, classification, severity, aggregation and risk-adjusted winability.
ownershipAndBoundaries.winningStrategy: Existing Rules Phase 8 and its configured engine remain authoritative for strategy recommendation and action generation.
ownershipAndBoundaries.aiReasoning: May interpret evidence and synthesize rationale under source constraints; may not fabricate evidence, override deterministic rules or infer unapproved crosswalk equivalence.

versionCompatibility.legacyDependencies: Preserve all existing v1.0 dependency references. Add the v1.1 assets as explicit additive dependencies; do not mass-replace frozen references.

parallelBranchesAfterEvidenceEvaluation: Existing PADF Phase 4 and Phase 5 branch
SWOT mapping, factor evaluation, gap management and TOWS branch
runtimeExecutionContracts.partialFailurePolicy: A failure isolated to the SWOT branch must not automatically invalidate otherwise valid existing pipeline assessment outputs. Existing v1.0 failure policies remain authoritative for existing phases.

evidenceToFactorMapping.mappingStrengthSemantics: Mapping relevance only; not evidence confidence, probability, evidence quality or runtime polarity.
applicabilityRequirements: Factor must be active in the resolved context.
Opportunity-specific evidence instance must actually be present.
Mapping scope must match the resolved context.
Factor evidence expectations must be checked.

runtimeRules.action: Retrieve approved KB v1.1 mapping records applicable to the resolved universal, revenue-motion and industry contexts. Do not copy or redefine mapping records in Rules.
Validate that each mapping evidenceObjectId resolves to the KB reusable evidence object catalogue and that a distinct opportunity evidence instance exists before treating it as evidence.
Resolve mapping factorId to a canonical factor definition in the active Industry Configuration context. Reject unresolved or inactive factor references.
Evaluate approved mapping applicability conditions, context scope, factor activation and factor evidence expectations. Reject context-incompatible mappings for this assessment.

Determine one eligible runtime relationship from the actual opportunity evidence instance and factor criteria. Do not infer the relationship from mapping strength or reusable evidence definition alone.
Determine POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, MIXED, NEUTRAL or UNDETERMINED polarity from actual opportunity evidence and context. Never assign fixed polarity to a reusable evidence object.
Record mappingId, evidenceObjectId, evidenceInstanceId, source and canonical factor IDs, mapping strength, applicability result, runtime relationship, polarity and rationale.

confidenceScaleSeparation.factorEvidenceConfidence: 1-5 ordinal; independently assessed against Industry Configuration criteria.
confidenceScaleSeparation.conversion: No direct mathematical conversion or automatic normalization.

factorAssessmentIntegration.compositeScorePolicy: Do not create a universal composite SWOT score. Use configured factor evaluation and priority governance.

runtimeRules.action: Initialize assessment records for the 16 active factors resolved from universal, revenue-motion and industry layers.
Resolve the factor-specific analytical criteria, evidence expectations and evaluation guidance from the active Industry Configuration factor definition.
Consolidate validated opportunity evidence with SUPPORTS relationships and applicable contextual evidence for the factor.
Evaluate CONTRADICTS, QUALIFIES and CONTEXTUALIZES evidence; preserve conflicting interpretations and do not suppress material counter-evidence.
Evaluate evidence quality and independently determine factor-level evidence_confidence on the configured 1–5 ordinal scale. Preserve KB evidence confidence 0–100 separately.
Assess the factor against its configured classification and criteria using evidence, context, uncertainty and counter-evidence. Do not infer factor classification from runtime polarity alone.
Determine factor priority using configured priority governance and mandatory considerations. Do not use a universal composite score.
Validate evidence lineage, evaluation dimensions, ordinal scale, rationale, uncertainty and factor lifecycle status before accepting the assessment.

evidenceGapManagement.unmappedHandling: Do not infer or force mappings. Use factor evidence expectations to request relevant opportunity evidence. A genuinely supplied evidence instance may be assessed through a separately governed unmapped-evidence path if supported by source rules.

runtimeRules.action: Identify missing_evidence and insufficient_evidence gaps against configured factor evidence expectations.
Identify conflicting_evidence, outdated_evidence and unverified_assumption gaps from evidence evaluation and factor reasoning.
Prioritize evidence gaps using configured strategic significance, priority and impact of missing evidence.
Generate information requirements and suggested questions from configured evidence expectations. Do not fabricate evidence or claim that requested evidence exists.
Identify affected factor assessments and initiate governed reassessment through Rules Phase 9 when new validated evidence materially changes the evidence basis.

eligibilityRequirements: Contributing factors must be active and evaluated.
Factor classifications must satisfy the configured TOWS combination.
Supporting evidence and mapping lineage must be traceable.
The strategic relationship must be meaningful and evidence-supported.
Feasibility, resources, timeframe and expected impact must be considered.
Unverified assumptions and material evidence gaps must remain visible.

runtimeRules.action: Identify relevant candidate combinations using active evaluated factors and the configured SO, WO, ST and WT definitions. Do not generate exhaustive or unsupported combinations.
Validate contributing factor classifications against the configured TOWS combination type.
Validate evidence support, provenance, recency, uncertainty and unresolved gaps for every contributing factor.
Evaluate strategic relevance and the causal or strategic relationship between contributing factors.
Evaluate feasibility, resource requirements, dependencies and execution constraints using configured guidance.
Describe expected strategic influence on winability without changing or replacing the authoritative winability calculation.
Determine an evidence- and context-supported execution timeframe without inventing a universal timeframe.
Prioritize eligible TOWS combinations using configured relevance, feasibility, urgency and strategic significance.
Detect duplicate or materially equivalent combinations while preserving distinct strategic rationales where justified.
Validate required strategy fields, factor and evidence references, strategy type, rationale and traceability against the approved SWOT schema and Industry Configuration contract.

riskIntelligenceCrosswalk.prohibition: Do not infer equivalence between KB risk trigger IDs, Industry risk pattern IDs and Rules risk rule IDs. Do not create duplicate risk records or duplicate risk calculations.

runtimeRules.action: Resolve only explicitly approved KB trigger to Industry risk pattern to Rules Phase 7 references. If no approved crosswalk exists, preserve an unresolved relationship diagnostic.
Validate the existence, semantics and context applicability of each risk trigger, risk pattern and Rules Phase 7 target.
Correlate relevant SWOT weaknesses and threats with existing authoritative risk records without creating a new risk event solely from a factor relationship.
Check existing risk identity and correlation references before passing contextual SWOT signals to the risk engine.
Pass validated evidence and SWOT context to existing Rules Phase 7 using its established risk input contract. Do not alter risk severity or aggregation logic.
Record crosswalk, risk trigger, risk pattern, Rules risk record and related SWOT factor references with mapping status.

strategyIdentifierLayers.kbStrategyCategoryIds: KB Phase 7 strategy categories WS_01 through WS_11
strategyIdentifierLayers.industryStrategyConfigurationIds: Industry Configuration strategy identifiers, including general and contextual identifiers

strategyCrosswalk.unmappedBehavior: Preserve TOWS candidate as unresolved strategic input; do not force assignment.

fieldTranslationContract.translation: Resolve only through approved strategy crosswalk.
Preserve as TOWS metadata; no direct target field established.
Preserve as strategic objective context; no direct target field established.
Translate only after semantic and value compatibility validation.
Translate action structure while preserving provenance.
Retain as additional strategy input; no direct target field established.
Translate only after semantic compatibility validation.
Map only approved compatible lifecycle states; otherwise reject handoff.

winningStrategyAdapter.unmappedTargetFieldsPolicy: Do not fabricate triggerCondition or executionOwner. Preserve existing configuration ownership and require target engine contract validation.

runtimeRules.action: Initialize strategy handoff for validated TOWS candidates.
Resolve the applicable KB strategy category associated with the TOWS candidate where an explicit source relationship exists.
Resolve Industry Configuration strategy ID only through an approved semantic crosswalk. Do not assume WS_01 equals WS01.
Validate crosswalk approval, strategy semantics, revenue-motion and industry applicability. Unmapped categories remain unresolved.
Validate all 13 required canonical strategy fields and all factor, evidence and TOWS references.
Translate only semantically compatible fields into the existing Winning Strategy engine input contract; preserve non-mappable fields as lineage/context metadata.
Validate required target fields, allowed values, trigger conditions and execution ownership using the existing engine contract. Reject unsupported or fabricated values.
Submit the validated payload to the existing Winning Strategy engine without replacing its recommendation, prioritization or action-generation logic.
Capture existing engine response identifiers, status, recommendations and execution references.
Preserve TOWS ID, KB category ID, Industry strategy ID, crosswalk version, adapter validation and resulting strategy/action references.

lifecycleIntegration.historicalSnapshotPolicy: Preserve prior assessment snapshots and trace records. Reassessment creates a new governed assessment revision or cycle; do not retroactively mutate historical results.

runtimeRules.action: Detect only approved material SWOT reassessment triggers and preserve trigger provenance.
Identify affected active factors from changed evidence, context and assessment dependencies; do not rerun all configured factors by default.
Identify TOWS combinations that reference affected factors or evidence.
Identify existing risk and strategy records linked to affected factors and TOWS combinations.
Initiate reassessment through the existing Rules Phase 9 lifecycle and assessment-cycle governance.
Preserve previous factor assessments, evidence references, configuration versions and timestamps as immutable historical snapshots.
Track resulting TOWS and strategy changes with previous and current references through existing lifecycle governance.

auditAndTraceabilityIntegration.aiReasoningTracePolicy: Record concise decision-relevant rationale, evidence references, uncertainty, alternative interpretations and structured provenance. Do not treat hidden or unstructured model reasoning as the sole audit record.

runtimeRules.action: Initialize an assessment-scoped trace linked to opportunity, assessment and execution identifiers.
Record Rules, KB, Industry Configuration and schema versions plus dependency validation results.
Record evidence object and instance, mapping, source/canonical factor IDs, applicability, runtime relationship and polarity.
Record factor classification, evaluation dimensions, priority, evidence references, rationale and uncertainty.
Record gap ID, type, status, affected factor, evidence references and detection rationale.
Record TOWS ID, strategy type, contributing factors, evidence, mappings, rationale, feasibility and validation result.
Record base winability, risk evaluation, risk-adjusted winability and associated SWOT risk references.
Record KB strategy category, Industry strategy ID, crosswalk status/version, adapter validation, handoff and engine response.
Record reassessment trigger, affected factors, prior and current assessment references and lifecycle status.
Validate mandatory trace groups and ensure evidence-to-factor-to-TOWS-to-risk-to-strategy-to-action lineage is resolvable before finalization.

severityLevels.BLOCKING: Required dependency or contract cannot be satisfied; block dependent execution.
severityLevels.ERROR: Affected record or operation is invalid; reject affected record or operation.
severityLevels.WARNING: Output is incomplete or uncertain; continue only with explicit limitation.
severityLevels.INFO: Diagnostic or coverage observation; record and continue.

validationAndFailureGovernance.sourceStatusCompatibility: New severity levels are integration diagnostics and do not replace existing v1.0 execution-status or exception values.
backwardCompatibilityRequirements: Preserve existing v1.0 rule definitions and legacy IDs.
Preserve PADF scoring thresholds and calculations.
Preserve Phase 7 risk detection, severity and aggregation logic.
Preserve Phase 8 existing Winning Strategy functionality.
Preserve Phase 9 lifecycle and historical snapshot governance.
Preserve Phase 10 audit and governance controls.
Do not allow SWOT branch failure to automatically invalidate otherwise valid existing assessment outputs.

contextResolutionRules.action: Validate required KB v1.1, Industry Configuration v1.1 and SWOT Master Schema v1.0 dependencies before enabling the SWOT integration branch. Preserve all existing legacy dependencies.
Resolve revenue-motion source identifier using the explicit KB compatibility registry and retain both source and canonical IDs.
Resolve industry source identifier using the explicit KB compatibility registry and retain both source and canonical IDs.
Resolve active SWOT factor definitions using universal baseline, revenue-motion override and industry override precedence. Do not load the entire 96-factor catalogue as active factors.
Validate the resolved active factor set contains the configured universal baseline plus applicable revenue-motion and industry factors, expected 8+4+4=16, and that all factor IDs resolve.
